title: Barcelona’s Fermin Lopez to undergo surgery on right foot fracture, likely to miss World Cup
content:
Fermin Lopez is likely to miss the World Cup after sustaining a metatarsal fracture in his right foot that requires surgery.

The 23-year-old midfielder was taken off at half-time during Barcelona’s 3-1 win over Real Betis on Sunday and replaced by Alejandro Balde with hosts up by a single goal.

Barca announced on Monday that the 23-year-old midfielder will undergo surgery for a fifth-metatarsal fracture, while sources close to the player confirmed fears that the injury could rule him out of the World Cup. Spain’s squad for the tournament will be announced on Monday, May 25.

Fermin has been central figure in Barca’s La Liga-winning campaign, scoring 13 goals and providing 17 assists in 48 appearances across all competitions despite picking up two separate groin injuries.

The La Masia graduate was rewarded for his performances in January with a new contract, keeping him at Camp Nou until 2031.

Fermin has made seven senior appearances for Spain since his debut in 2024, appearing in three of this season’s World Cup qualifiers and both of Luis de la Fuente’s side’s March friendlies against Serbia and Egypt, providing one assist.

The World Cup would have been his second major tournament after the 2024 European Championship, though he only managed 28 minutes on their way to overall victory.

Spain are first in action during this summer’s tournament on June 15, taking on Cape Verde, before matches against Saudi Arabia on June 21 and Uruguay on June 27.

Analysis by Barcelona correspondent Laia Cervello Herrero

The fact that Fermin Lopez is likely to miss the World Cup is a major blow for Spain.

He would be competing for the position with Dani Olmo, but the 23-year-old’s season with Barcelona has meant that Olmo is no longer a guaranteed starter at the club, and Luis De La Fuente has certainly taken note.

Fermin is one of the midfielders with the highest goals-per-game average in Europe. He has been involved in 30 goals for Barcelona — 13 goals and 17 assists — and was in excellent form.

He is a player who contributes a great deal to the team, both as a starter and as a substitute. Fermin is a fiercely competitive player who takes risks in front of goal; he is intense, electric, helps with the press and can also play as a left winger. His versatility is crucial as Nico Williams’ inclusion in the squad remains in doubt.

Together with Olmo, they give the manager two different options depending on what the match requires at that moment.

Losing this player would be a blow for Spain as he has been one of the most in-form midfielders heading into the World Cup.
